parsed.explanation: The combined regime pairs a federal document/entry regime (X markers barred, M/F-only processing, a cable directing refusal where documents cast doubt on sex, possible fraud-based lifetime ineligibility, reported blocked passports) with a state facility statute covering airports, parks, courts, schools and jails, enforced by criminal trespass with one documented arrest and 24-hour men's-ward detention. Compounding: adult and minor care restrictions, conscience refusals, no state discrimination or hate-crime coverage, two organization travel advisories, hostile federal framing, and public support for birth-sex markers. Mitigation is real but partial: private businesses are out of scope, the sole prosecution was dismissed, courts enjoined care bans, and litigation continues. Several distinct punitive provisions compound, holding this in Elevated Risk.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal order bars X markers and self-selection; Feb 2025 cable instructs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and consideration of fraud-based lifetime ineligibility; travelers report passports blocked or confiscated; state treats mismatched licence markers as fraud.
entry_documents.protection: Existing X-marker passports valid to expiry; ACLU suit pending; legal-aid FAQ tracks the rules; lifetime bar requires four elements and is never automatic.
entry_documents.interaction: Border document doubt feeds directly into the state's assigned-sex-only licence regime and facility rules during any secondary screening or stop.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: State trespass charge carries up to 60 days; documented arrest of a trans student held 24 hours in the men's ward; federal corrections conversion-therapy-style policies (hair, hormones, psychiatric drugs); immigration custody reports of beatings, solitary and sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: The single state case was dismissed on standing; no later arrest documented; habeas and litigation channels function.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Facility refusal-to-depart converts a bathroom visit into arrest and birth-sex holding, the same pathway that runs into federal custody practices.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: State statute bars congruent restroom/changing use in all state, local and school buildings including airports, parks, beaches, jails and immigration detention; authority figure may order departure; criminal trespass follows refusal; four jurisdictions criminalise in some circumstances.
federal_state_facilities.protection: Private businesses expressly out of scope; offence requires willful entry plus refusal to depart, not automatic arrest; exemptions listed.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Airport facility exclusion combines with federal document screening, so the traveller meets both regimes at the same journey stage.

care_services.exposure: State bars minors' blockers/hormones/surgery, imposes 24-hour adult waiting period, physicians-only rule displacing ~80% of clinic patients, conscience-refusal law reaching all patients, and insurance exclusions; federal proposed rule would bar public insurance for under-18s.
care_services.protection: National judge permanently blocked minors and adults provisions June 2024; three-plaintiff injunction earlier; emergency care not documented as refused.
care_services.interaction: Conscience refusal and physicians-only rules reach a visiting adult or travelling child directly, while the injunction's appellate status is unresolved.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Federal counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' groups; DOJ reward memo invokes 'radical gender ideology'; January 2025 orders and removal of trans materials; 66% public support for birth-sex document laws; two organization travel advisories and a Do Not Travel label.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Reward memo never lists gender ideology as a reward criterion; the strategy disclaims targeting mere disagreement; national hate-crime statute covers gender identity.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Official framing raises both street hostility and the probability of discretionary scrutiny or outing by officers and staff.

minors_guardians.exposure: State minor care ban, sports exclusion, custody-modification provisions on a child's receipt of gender-affirming care, federal order criminalising teachers facilitating social transition, and a schools clause purporting to cover private schools; DEI/gender-identity funding ban from Jan 2027.
minors_guardians.protection: June 2024 permanent block of care bans (appellate status unresolved); same-sex marriage lawful since 2015.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling family faces care denial for the child and potential state inquiry if the child socially transitions, even though the parent commits no offence.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: 3.7 trans women murdered per 100k per year and a Do Not Travel label; no state gender-identity discrimination or hate-crime coverage; only 23 jurisdictions cover gender identity in bias-crime statutes; national analysis finds law severity does not correlate with killing rates.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute and 2020 employment ruling apply; cities covering ~55% of population ban gender-identity discrimination; human-relations commission enforces.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Because violence is documented as independent of legal climate, court remedies do not offset the street-level risk; the denominator versus background homicide is unstated.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Facility statute never substantively tested; appellate status of care rules, licence/birth-certificate rules and travel advisories unresolved; airport application of the facility law undocumented; no state discrimination statute.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Prosecution dismissed; multiple injunctions and a pending ACLU suit; running legal-aid FAQ; functioning courts that have granted trans relief.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Recourse operates in part, but the operative document, facility and care rules remain in force while litigation proceeds.

anchor_checks.comparison: That anchor has birth-sex prison placement as routine, cross-dressing criminalised in administrative buildings, slow remedies and discouraged reporting. Ours shares the tier-1 facility-by-birth-sex exclusion and a documented arrest with men's-ward holding, but sits higher: only one prosecution in three years, private premises untouched, and courts that dismiss, enjoin and entertain suit. Less pervasive custody harm, similar state-imposed exposure.

Similar structure: universal visitor-facing exclusions (facility and document regimes), care denial reaching nonresidents and minors, and remedies limited to apologies or future policy review. Ours adds criminal trespass with actual detention and hostile federal framing, so slightly lower; it also has broader private-space freedom and working injunctions, which that anchor lacks. Comparable tier.

That anchor has trained respectful border officers, brief detention ending in release, written reasons, counsel access and compensation. Here the entry regime mandates refusal on sex doubt with possible lifetime ineligibility, passports are reported blocked, and facility use in airports is criminally chargeable. Nothing comparable to written reasons or compensation exists; markedly lower.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller meets one system: federal document and entry rules that presume a fixed birth sex and instruct refusal on doubt, running into a state facility statute that criminalises congruent use across every government building including airports, with a documented arrest and men's-ward holding as proof the pathway executes. Care is restricted for adults and minors with only partial, unsettled injunctive relief; no state discrimination or hate-crime coverage exists, and official framing plus two travel advisories elevate scrutiny. Mitigation is genuine but bounded: private businesses are outside the statute, the lone prosecution collapsed on standing, national employment and hate-crime law still apply, and litigation continues. Several distinct punitive provisions compound against the federal tier, keeping this in Elevated Risk rather than Reduced Risk.
